sourcedFrom: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: The 92XI is a single-action 92 on a Vertec frame, and it strips exactly like the rest of the line: lever, slide, spring, barrel. The recoil spring and its guide are the parts that end up under the bench, so work over a table and let the spring out slowly.

steps.title: Unloaded before the lever is touched
steps.action: Magazine out, slide back, chamber looked at and felt. The disassembly lever rotates on a loaded pistol exactly as it does on an empty one — the gun gives you no signal, so the check is the signal.
steps.quote: MAKE SURE THE PISTOL IS UNLOADED. IF NOT, UNLOAD
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — Field Stripping, printed p.18-19

steps.title: Magazine out, then hold the lever release button in
steps.action: Drop the magazine with the release catch, then press and HOLD the disassembly lever release button while you rotate the lever. Holding it is the part people skip, and then they think the lever is seized.
steps.aside: Press and hold the disassembly lever release button.
steps.quote: Remove magazine by depressing magazine release catch.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — Field Stripping, printed p.18-19

steps.title: Slide assembly forward off the frame
steps.action: With the lever turned, run the slide assembly straight forward off the frame rails — barrel, locking block, recoil spring and guide all still inside it.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — Field Stripping, printed p.18-19

steps.title: ⛔ Spring and guide are under tension — ease them out
steps.action: Press the recoil spring and spring guide slightly toward the MUZZLE to separate them from the barrel, then lift the guide and let the spring out slowly. Let go of it and it goes across the room; that is the whole reason Beretta prints the caution.
steps.aside: Lift the spring guide and recoil spring, letting the spring out slowly, as it is under tension.
steps.quote: Recoil spring and recoil spring guide are under tension. Slightly press recoil spring and spring guide towards muzzle to separate them from the barrel.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — Field Stripping, printed p.18-19

steps.title: Barrel and locking block out — strip complete
steps.action: Lift the barrel with its locking block assembly out of the slide. Four groups on the bench and that is the end of the published strip — Beretta recommends anything further be a gunsmith's job.
steps.aside: Beretta recommends any further disassembly be performed by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel and locking block assembly from slide.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — Field Stripping, printed p.18-19

steps.title: Barrel outside first, then oil the lug and locking block
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the barrel, locking block and lug assembly with a solvent-soaked patch, let it dry, then lubricate the lug and locking block area — that is the surface doing the unlocking work. Light oil inside and outside the barrel afterwards.
steps.aside: Lightly oil the inside and outside of the barrel, using a clean patch soaked in gun oil. Lightly oil the locking block.
steps.quote: Wipe down exterior of barrel locking block and lug assembly with a solvent soaked patch. Allow to dry, then apply lubrication in the lug and locking block area.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Slide: breech face, extractor, rails, underside of the breech
steps.action: Cloth or brush soaked in gun oil over the slide, with attention to the breech face, extractor, slide rails and the underside of the breech. Wipe clean, oil lightly, and put a few drops down the rails.
steps.aside: Lightly oil the slide. Apply a few drops of oil down the rails of the slide.
steps.quote: Clean the slide with a cloth and/or brush soaked in gun oil, paying special attention to the breech face, extractor, slide rails and under side of breech.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Frame, and the levers in front of the hammer
steps.action: Oil-soaked rag or brush over every area carrying powder residue, wipe clean, then lightly lubricate the rails and the moving parts Beretta names: disassembly lever, magazine catch, slide stop, trigger system, hammer, sear, and the levers in front of the hammer.
steps.quote: Wipe clean and lightly lubricate rails and moving parts. Be sure to oil the disassembly lever, magazine catch, slide stop, trigger system, hammer, sear and the levers in front of the hammer.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Magazines, and rotate carry ammunition
steps.action: Clean the magazines thoroughly and wipe them with a lightly oiled rag. If the pistol is carried loaded, unload the magazines periodically and look at the cartridges — a round that has been chambered repeatedly is not the round you want under a firing pin.
steps.aside: If the pistol is carried with chamber and magazine loaded, it is important to periodically unload all magazines for cartridge inspection.
steps.quote: Be sure to thoroughly clean the magazine(s). After cleaning, wipe with a lightly oil moistened rag.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20-21

steps.title: Grip panels: 2 mm Allen, and 10 lb·in going back
steps.action: If the grips come off for a deep clean, a 2 mm Allen wrench turns the screws counter-clockwise — and mind the lock washers underneath, which are easy to lose and not optional. Back on, they torque to 10 lb·in: snug, not gorilla-tight.
steps.aside: Install the lock washers and grip screws with a 2 mm allen wrench by turning them clockwise. Tighten the grip screws to a torque of 10 lb·in.
steps.quote: Using a 2 mm allen wrench, remove the grip screws by turning them counterclockwise.
steps.cite: Beretta 92XI User Manual — UD6A0575 rev 2 (form code printed in the running header) — Grip Panels Remove and Install, printed p.20

deepAbsentReason: Beretta stops the owner at the field strip on this pistol and says so twice: "Beretta recommends any further disassembly be performed by a qualified gunsmith" at the end of the strip, and "The firearm should not be disassembled for cleaning beyond what is described. Only gunsmiths or other highly-trained personnel who are familiar with these firearms should conduct further disassembly." in maintenance. The grip-panel removal is published and rides as a cleaning step, but it is not a deeper strip. A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing deeper is borrowed from anywhere else.

cleaning.name: BARREL & LOCKING BLOCK
tasks: Solvent patch over the exterior, dried, then lube on the lug and locking block area
Light oil inside and outside the barrel

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Breech face, extractor, rails and underside of the breech
Wipe clean, light oil, a few drops down the rails

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Powder residue off every surface it has reached
Light lube on the rails, disassembly lever, magazine catch, slide stop, trigger system, hammer, sear and the levers in front of the hammer

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES & CARRY AMMUNITION
tasks: Magazines cleaned, then wiped with a lightly oiled rag
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges
If carried loaded, unload the magazines periodically and inspect

reassembly: Barrel and locking block into the slide, extractor lying in its groove in the barrel.
Recoil spring onto its guide, guide head into the centre of its groove in the locking block.
Slide assembly onto the frame rails, pushed back to or beyond the rear of the frame.
⛔ Rotate the disassembly lever back ONLY with the slide closed and aligned.
Cycle the slide, function check, and confirm the safety operates before loading.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: verify the safety, insert an EMPTY magazine and retract the slide so it stays open, then pull it back and release it to close. Cycle it a few more times and confirm it returns fully into battery. Rotate the disassembly lever only with the slide closed and aligned.
